**From:** {{< meta from-address >}}  
**Manuscript Location:** {{< meta manuscript-location >}}  

My dear [Miss Smith](../persons.html#263)
Thanks for the Exhibition - which is full of interest. I wish there was any chance of my seeing it. I like most of what you have said much, though I do not agree with your deprecation of [Dr Hook](../persons.html#709)’s character of Edward VI, for certainly his own journal does not bear out the praises bestowed on him, and it was rather forward to say the least of it in a mere boy to meddle with the convictions of learned men.

Thanks much for the whole - it is pleasant reading-
[The rest of the letter is missing]

[^1]: The paper has been cut about to remove the signature, address and date.

[^2]: A.

Carter Smith’s article ‘National Portrait Gallery’ appeared in MP 1868 (2): 65.

[^3]: Walter Farquhar Hook wrote The Three Reformations (1847), Lives of the Archbishops of Canterbury (1862) and A Church Dictionary (1864, 9th ed.)
